name: MD-02
label: Safe D

key_factors: District leans Democratic by 10 points on the partisan baseline
Incumbent Johnny Olszewski has a massive fundraising edge ($1.04M raised vs. $20K)
Prediction markets price Democratic win odds around 94%
model.rationale: The fundamentals point strongly to Olszewski: a Democratic-leaning district, incumbency, and a fundraising advantage of roughly 50-to-1, with markets also pricing this as near-certain for Democrats. With no polls or expert ratings to contradict that picture, the forecast stays at Safe D.
model.watch: Any late polling showing a much tighter race or unexpected outside spending against Olszewski would be the first sign of movement.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Maryland's 2nd District is a Democratic-leaning seat, and first-term incumbent Johnny Olszewski is running for reelection with every structural advantage. He has raised over $1 million and holds more than $600,000 on hand, while Republican Dave Wallace has raised about $20,000 with minimal cash remaining. No outside groups are spending against the incumbent.

No public general-election polls cover the race, and no expert raters have weighed in, so the outlook rests on district fundamentals, money, and prediction markets, which price a Democratic win at roughly 94%. The expected margin is about 21 points, consistent with a Safe D rating, though uncertainty is somewhat elevated given the absence of polling.
